$purpose: The governance ledger for dependencies that functions/index.js requires but the deploy
tree does not carry. The gate reads this to report WHY each one is missing and WHO must
decide, instead of collapsing four different situations into the word 'missing'.
EDITING THIS FILE IS A GOVERNANCE ACT, NOT CONFIGURATION.
It records decisions that have already been taken. It does not take them, and adding a
row here does NOT make anything deployable: the gate reads `git ls-tree`, not this file,
to decide whether the tree closes. A disposition recorded here is a decision RECORDED,
not a dependency RESOLVED. Only committed deploy-tree content, or an explicit tested
removal of the require/export, closes the gate.

$statuses.RESOLVED: Provenance established and the module is committed to this branch. If a RESOLVED entry is ever missing from the tree, that is a REGRESSION and the gate says so.
$statuses.GATED: Real, wanted work that is deliberately held back behind a documented prerequisite. Retain; do not remove.
$statuses.UNRESOLVED: Required by the tracked index.js, but nobody has attributed or authorised it. Needs a decision from an owner.
$statuses.FOREIGN_PORT: Committed on another lineage; this branch does not carry it. Needs lineage reconciliation before admission.

functions/tenant-identity.summary: Committed at 24f50ba, byte-identical to the blob at 25d2c19 (sha1 4d89a1da854f8a05e41147661dfff42654a4bf3b). Five consumers resolve against it.

functions/order-claim.summary: Unresolved provenance, but TECHNICALLY EVIDENCED. A dedicated trace exists (8796777) and a companion concurrency test passes 27/0 against a live Firestore emulator. What is missing is governance, not working code.
functions/order-claim.ownerNote: Do not infer an owner from commits, file authorship, or adjacent work — no record anywhere establishes who authorised it.
functions/order-claim.path: Attribute the work, then admit it: commit the module TOGETHER WITH scripts/test-order-claim-race.js. Only if the feature is genuinely unwanted: an explicit, tested removal of its require/export.
functions/order-claim.forbidden: Do NOT delete it to make this gate green. Absence of an owner is not evidence a feature is unwanted, and a red gate is not a reason to destroy a demonstrated, transactionally safe capability.

functions/manual-till-orders.summary: Retain. checkout.html:1875 calls createManualTillOrder on a live page, and functions/checkout-mode.js deliberately returns manual_payment_unavailable until the lifecycle ships. The gate there is designed to be flipped, not removed.
functions/manual-till-orders.ownerNote: The manual-till lifecycle workstream. Not named here because no record assigns an individual.
functions/manual-till-orders.path: Certify the production order lifecycle (createManualTillOrder + attestManualTillPayment), keep manual_payment OFF until then, then commit.
functions/manual-till-orders.forbidden: Do NOT remove: a live customer-facing page calls it. Do NOT enable manual_payment before its lifecycle certification.

functions/commission-invoice.summary: Canonical and already certified 52/0, but deliberately not deployable: 'BUILT 52/0 · NOT DEPLOYED · NO INVOICE CAN ISSUE'. Blocked by configuration and business decisions, not by code quality.
functions/commission-invoice.ownerNote: Decision-holder is whoever owns revenueConfig/commission_vat and the two open business decisions. Not named here because no record assigns an individual.
functions/commission-invoice.path: Set revenueConfig/commission_vat, resolve the two outstanding business decisions, then commit.
functions/commission-invoice.forbidden: Do NOT weaken the gate to accommodate it, and do NOT deploy it before its configuration exists — no invoice may issue against an unset VAT policy.

functions/pos-mpesa-refs.summary: Proven foreign port, certified 57/0 on its own lineage. Committed at 233ac4d and present on other branches; this branch does not carry it.
functions/pos-mpesa-refs.ownerNote: Whoever owns that port's integration into this lineage. Not named here because no record assigns an individual.
functions/pos-mpesa-refs.path: Reconcile the foreign-port lineage and intended integration, then explicitly admit or explicitly remove.
functions/pos-mpesa-refs.forbidden: Do NOT copy it into this branch on the strength of a byte-identical blob existing elsewhere. Provenance and intended integration must be reconciled first.
